review_text:
This restaurant really is a great place for a special dinner.

I had recently attended a small dinner commemorating my friend’s birthday. When we arrived, we were quickly lead to our table upstairs. The restaurant was to my surprise fairly quiet for a Friday night.

The menu is organized well with many choices fitting for anyones taste. Additionally there is a note at the bottom that suggests the chefs could take custom requests, however no one at my table took advantage of this.

We had ordered a pizza to share and a pasta each.

The pizza was thin and crispy with the perfect amount of cheese, which beat the taste of the advertised vodka sauce.

My dish which name I do not recall was great, hot pasta with great sauce. There were no complaints about the food at my table. The lasagna received the most compliments.
After our meal, we received a plate of Italian pastry with powdered sugar sprinkled on top.

The staff were great as well however I have a small gripe. At one point while my water was being refilled, it spilled onto the table. This is not a big deal however something to note.

With the atmosphere the restaurant is  well decorated with memorabilia from the Sopranos 25th anniversary, which was hosted at this restaurant. Something that caught my eye was the brick work, the bottom floor is seen to have old red clay bricks, seeing the wear and tear over time. When rising to the second floor, the bricks sharply change to obviously newly laid bricks. Looking at a half arch that was across our table, I noticed the brick work gets cut iff sharply, with the side brick not shown. This to me suggests that the brick work on that part is not real bricks. I have no way to confirm this but it was slightly disappointing for me.

I definitely recommend checking this place out, it will be a strong contender for me in the future and my time in the city of New York.

review_text: I was quite excited to try this spa and booked a 6pm 90 min massage plus pool experience with a friend once we had her baby sitter firmed up. My friend got there a little early and waited for me in the reception area as we weren't allowed to enter the women's locker room until after 5:45pm, 15 mins before our massage. Check-in was hassle free and the women's locker room was fine, nothing luxurious but had what you need (the attendant was very helpful). We went down to the massage area and were greeted there by two staff who told us we would get a tour of the pool area once our massages were done. I was impressed with my massage therapist but was surprised my friend and I were out in the same room given we didn't book a couples massage, just booked two massages under one booking as I've often done at other luxury spas. Once the massage was finished we asked to get a tour of the facility and were directed to the upper pools near the massage area first. These were very nice and we were looking forward to our full 1.25 hours. Nothing from staff to indicate there would be any issue in fact they said to come get them when we were ready for the tour of the other part of the facility. At around 8pm (30 mins in to our facility time) we were told we have to leave as some influencers will be filming and had booked the whole facility. Until this time no one had told us this would be happening and I had only received emails to arrive by 5:45 for the massage and spa facility I had paid up front for, for two people. My friend and I were very confused and were told to go speak to the manager which we did. This manager had the worst customer service attitude. She didn't apologize to start and instead was fixated on trying to prove we probably had our whole experience but she also took a mbout 10 mins to do her math looking at a computer screen and asking us multiple times when we got there, when we started , how we started even though both the emails and the front desk had been clear massage first and rest of spa facility after that. When we pressed for reasons why we weren't told she tried to insinuate we probably had been which my friend and I firmly explained had not happened at any time before or after we arrived. She then shared the only thing she could offer is was give us a credit for unused spa time - and at this point let's be clear I'm never using any Aire spa anywhere ever again and neither is my friend. Well, we were finally able to get an actual monetary refund for time unused but only after we had to request this several times. When I asked the front desk why they hadn't said anything at 5:45 all I got was there was a miscommunication and only people that started arriving at 7pm were told. The front desk were a lot more apologetic than the manager. Well I hope the influencers were worth the customers the company lost that day.

★★★★★ An Exceptional French Dining Experience in NYC

Le Coucou continues to be one of my favorite restaurants in New York City, consistently delivering an extraordinary dining experience where exquisite French cuisine, impeccable service, and an intimate, refined atmosphere come together beautifully.

We began with the Thon à l’Espelette, wonderfully fresh and perfectly balanced, with delicate flavors that complemented the tuna beautifully.

The Tartare de Bœuf, prepared with prime filet and crowned with a generous layer of caviar and a golden egg yolk, was fantastic. Rich, elegant, and beautifully presented, it was an indulgent interpretation of a French classic.

However, the undisputed star of the evening was the grilled foie gras. Beautifully crosshatched, expertly seared, and cooked to absolute perfection, it delivered an extraordinary combination of flavor, richness, and texture. Simply delicious and the ultimate gourmandise. A dish worth returning for on its own.

For our main courses, we enjoyed the Canette aux Figues, which was outstanding. The duck was perfectly cooked, exceptionally tender and juicy, with beautifully balanced flavors. It was easily the second-best dish of the evening, surpassed only by the remarkable foie gras.

We also had the Côte de Veau Gratinée aux Cèpes, a beautifully prepared, tender veal chop. The porcini mushroom gratin was absolutely phenomenal, adding remarkable depth and richness that elevated the entire dish.

Although we skipped dessert, we were graciously treated to freshly baked madeleines and an assortment of delicate mignardises—a thoughtful and elegant conclusion to the meal.

We ended the evening with two exceptionally crafted espresso martinis, prepared with freshly brewed espresso and shaken to perfection. A wonderful final touch.

The service was exceptional, as it has been on our previous visits—attentive, polished, and effortlessly professional.

The atmosphere is simply unmatched. The intimate, sophisticated dining room features beautifully balanced lighting that subtly illuminates each table without ever becoming intrusive. Every detail contributes to an ambiance that feels both luxurious and genuinely welcoming.

Le Coucou remains one of my absolute favorite restaurants in NYC. A truly five-star dining experience that continues to impress, visit after visit.

★★★★★
Le Petit Nissa – A Little Slice of the French Riviera in SoHo!
Every once in a while, you stumble upon a restaurant that reminds you why dining out can be such a wonderful experience. Le Petit Nissa is one of those places.
I happened to walk by during the day on Friday and noticed this beautiful new restaurant. I stopped in, met the owner, and we had a lovely conversation. I asked if there was any chance he could accommodate my wife and me for dinner that evening. He graciously found us a table for 6:30 on a Friday night, which I really appreciated.
From the moment we walked in, we felt like we had been transported to a little village in the South of France. The restaurant is intimate, beautifully designed, simple, elegant, and understated. I love restaurants of this size, especially in a city filled with enormous dining rooms. What struck me was that although Le Petit Nissa had only been open for a week or two, it already had the soul of a neighborhood institution that had been there for generations. There’s something very special about that.
Now, the food!
We started with the French baguette and butter and the Provençal mussels. Sometimes the simplest things are the most memorable. The bread and butter were so wonderful that I could have been sitting at a little café on the French Riviera. The mussels were absolutely beautiful, prepared with garlic and parsley butter, almost reminiscent of a classic escargot preparation. Perfectly seasoned, delicate, and absolutely delicious.
For our entrées, my wife had the Pâtes au Pistou, fresh pasta with Parmigiano Reggiano, basil, and pine nuts. It was delicate, beautifully balanced, and cooked to perfection. The portion was just right, and the simplicity of the dish was what made it so special.
I ordered the steak frites, and I don’t say this lightly: it was one of the best I’ve ever had. The steak was perfectly cooked, beautifully portioned, and served with compound butter and garlic confit. And those skinny, hand-cut fries! Quite possibly the best fries I’ve ever eaten. Nothing overcomplicated, just beautiful ingredients prepared with care. Perfection.
We finished by sharing the mousse au chocolat with Chantilly cream, olive oil, and sea salt. I have enjoyed chocolate mousse in many restaurants over the years, but this was hands down the best I’ve ever had. The texture was heavenly, the Chantilly cream was whipped to perfection, and the drizzle of beautiful olive oil with a touch of Maldon sea salt brought everything together. An absolutely stunning dessert.
But what really made the evening special was the feeling of the place. The dining room was buzzing, yet somehow it felt relaxed and comfortable. The service was impeccable without being the least bit stuffy.
I loved watching the owner work the room. He was everywhere, greeting guests, checking on tables, helping his staff, and making sure everything ran smoothly. You could see how much heart he was putting into his restaurant.
And I have to mention the young woman chef running the kitchen. I had the pleasure of watching her work, and it was like watching a beautifully choreographed dance. With her assistants around her, she was so focused, calm, and precise, orchestrating everything with remarkable confidence. It was genuinely impressive and a pleasure to watch.
I almost hesitated to write this review because a part of me wanted to keep this little gem a secret! But places like Le Petit Nissa deserve to be celebrated.
To the owner, the chef, and everyone who made our Friday evening so memorable, thank you. You’ve created something really special, and I wish you nothing but success. I have a feeling this little restaurant is going to become a beloved part of the neighborhood.
The secret is officially out!
We’ll be back very soon… assuming we can still get a table! LOL.
All the best and much continued success!

review_text:
Il Cortile is one of the restaurants that still represents the older character of Manhattan's Little Italy. Operating since 1975, it has a traditional Italian dining atmosphere that feels very different from the newer restaurants in Nolita. The most interesting feature is the glass-ceilinged garden dining room, which creates a sense of openness despite being surrounded by the buildings of Lower Manhattan.

The fettuccine di Parma is one of the dishes worth knowing about. It's a rich pasta preparation where the texture of the noodles and the consistency of the sauce are particularly important. Rather than relying on an enormous quantity of ingredients, the dish follows the traditional Italian approach of combining pasta with a carefully prepared sauce.

The restaurant's menu concentrates on Italian classics, including pasta, seafood and meat dishes. The setting makes it especially suitable for a longer family dinner rather than a quick meal between sightseeing stops.

One thing worth considering is where you sit. The garden room offers a noticeably different atmosphere from the front dining area. The restaurant also has several private dining spaces, so larger groups can be accommodated without necessarily occupying the main dining room.

Mulberry Street becomes extremely crowded during weekends and festivals, and the surrounding noise is part of the neighbourhood's character. Il Cortile is particularly interesting for people who want a traditional Italian-American dining experience in a restaurant with genuine neighbourhood history.

review_text:
Love the atmosphere and aesthetic of this spot. It was a great date night! The concept is fun and different, and I enjoyed being able to pick out my own wine, cheese, and meats from the fridge. That said there were a few things I didn’t realize until I visited that made the experience feel a bit limiting.

I was surprised to see individual packages of meat from Trader Joe’s priced at $12, with each variety sold separately. I would love the option to tell the server curating the board how many varieties we’d like for two people and have them put something together accordingly. As it stands, the individual pricing makes it easy to overspend and end up with more food than you need.

The flow also felt a little disjointed. After selecting your items, you bring everything to the end of the bar (I felt in the way of other guests who were seated bc you’re kind of standing directly in front of their tables), pay, and hand it off to the servers to plate. The service felt a bit hands-off, too, as the servers didn’t really check in throughout the experience.

They don’t do wine by the glass, so it can feel like a lot for two people. I understand the concept is different from a traditional wine bar, just wanted to share!!

Overall, it’s a fun spot with a great aesthetic and something different to offer! I just wish there was more flexibility with the food options, pricing, and service.

review_text:
All the cats are so sweet, friendly, and full of energy. The space is super clean, and there are three areas to explore: the main floor, outdoor patio, and basement. You can really tell the staff love the cats and take such good care of them.

As a matcha cafe, they use single-origin Yame matcha from Fukuoka. Yame is actually my favorite matcha, and there aren't many spots in NYC that serve it! I loved it so much that I immediately picked up a tin to take home. It even comes in the cutest little cat-shaped container.

The black sesame matcha latte was SO GOOD! Both the black sesame and matcha flavors were rich. I'd come back even just for the drinks alone!

Their matcha is on the pricier side, but a portion of the sales goes to animal welfare charities, so you're also supporting a good cause while enjoying some matcha and cat time.

The cafe and cat areas are actually separate, so you can totally just grab a matcha and hang out in the cafe without going into the cat area.

review_text:
As a big fan of Kokoro cat cafe in flushing, I had to check out their Les Location asap!!!

This spot used to be a cat cafe before it became Kokoro cat cafe's second location.  They partner with the same Anjellicle Cats Rescue as kokoro. I had always loved this location because of their 3 story design. The cat has alot of cozy space to explore! Two indoor space and one outdoor space! The outdoor space is so loved by the cats back then and now!

I loved how clean and cozy Kokoro kept their cat cafes. Dragon, the owner definitely is someone who pay attention to details! The space feel extra cozy now with the light interior that mimick the cat cafes in Japan! Cat loves the colors of nature. There is alot of green and blue decorations, pillow and furniture at Kokoro! Its very intentional and makes the cats very happy. Its not just asthetic ♡

The best part of cat cafes are definitely the cats! Kokoro lower east side have so many calicos! So amazing!

MY FAVORITE CAT AT KOKORO les is definitely Alana & Ernie. All the calicos honestly  HAHAAHAH! They are all so curious and loves humans.

Alana (Calico) is a very territorial cat, She will want to fight the other cats to keep you to herself! She loves getting attention from people! SHE GOT THE BIGGEST BOBA EYES, IT TOTUALLY MELT ME!

Ernie (Ginger) is a love bug. He kinda look like a fox if you put his ears down LOL! He is so chill and always want to snuggle! Please give him head pats when you visit because he will melt into your lap!

Katie (calico) is also a love bug! She is so so chill, she flops herself into laps and does a stretches in people's lap to make herself comfortable. Can't wait for kokoro les to host cat yoga sessions, Katie can be the cat leader of these sessions hahaha!

Sabbi and Bert always walk together ♡
They look so identical, I was seeing double
Their fur color are exactly the same. Their face look alittle different. Sabbi is chubbier then Bert. Sabbi will find her way into your lab to snuggle while  Bert is very playful and apprently a foot licker... Watch out! Bert might get your foot aahha

Beside the cats, their Croissants and Matchas are so GOOOOD! I tried their almond croissant today. Came in with no expectation for the food but now I am raving to my friends how good everything is! Their matcha line is so cute! THE TIN CAN IS LITERALLY CAT!!!! Its not just cute to look at but the matcha actually taste so perfect! I have to say, I am very picky with my pastries and matchas! I only have a few matcha spot i would recommend to people. Good matchas are really hard to come by! Dragon said they source their from Japan! I definitely can taste it hahaha! I usually take my time drinking anything but it was so good!! I try to savor it but I finished it in 4 min LOL! I got the coconut matcha! I am alittle bias bc I love coconut in anything! I really wanted to order a second matcha. It took so much self control to not get another one.

This review is getting way too wordy and long but if you made it this far....

Interior 100/10
Cats 10000000/10
Food and Drink 10000000/10
Cleanliness: 100/10

Oh they even got these new freeze dry cat lolipops! My friend also give her cats freeze dry lolipops, cats loves them so much. They are crazy for them! They are part of their premium package. The premium package comes with a cat lolipop, a polaroid photo and THEIR MATCHA DRINKS!

I wish kokoro all the success in this new location!!! Dragon and their team are cat lovers! They're very intentional and cares deeply about their cats! When cats are deeply loved, they become sweet love bugs

review_text:
The PUBLIC hotel is incredible, I believe it truly caters to all needs. We stayed in Queen Hi-Floor rooms which were a perfect size for a six night trip.

The hotel is a great location, in-between all the major shops of 5th Avenue etc and downtown Manhattan. Expect to be walking a lot in NYC :)

Unfortunately on our last night, one of our party had a medical emergency and being from the UK and unfamiliar with the US medical system, the hotel staff were incredible in helping us, they accommodated all of our needs and were so supportive in the midst of a crisis. I especially want to mention Lasandra, Jonathan, and both reception teams who were there on the evening of the 15th and morning of the 16th. I wouldn't have been able to navigate such a difficult situation without their help and I will be forever grateful they were there.

On the note of your staff, I also had the pleasure of meeting Ella and Solana, in both the rooftop bar and the downstairs bar behind the pool table. They were so hospitable, and such lovely girls!! Unfortunately I had the unpleasant experience of running into quite a rude and aggressive patron of the downstairs bar, behind the pool table. From what I could understand this man was not a guest of the hotel and was being incredibly rude to bar tender on duty that night and her bar back (I didn't catch their names). I complained about this behaviour to the bar manager that night, I believe their name is Jay and said I would like this person removed for being so disgustingly rude to their staff there, of which Jay refused to do. I understand situations like that need to be handled carefully, however from my own observations I could tell the staff behind the bar that night were uncomfortable with this man and I believe Jay did not look out for his staff appropriately and this should be addressed internally.

Overall, my family and I had the most incredible time in NYC and our stay at The PUBLIC hotel was everything we had hoped for and more.

We will be returning.

Kindest, Stella

review_text:
**Heavy on style, light on amenities**

Everything at the Public screams "Design," and some of it is genuinely good. Our corner loft room was spacious, with a beautiful exposed concrete ceiling and dramatic views. But the yellow, semi-transparent glass toilet enclosure offered little privacy, and closet space was tight for one of the largest room categories. There's no room service, no turndown service, no coffee machine and no minibar, just a small, empty fridge.

The WeWork-style lobby is open to the public and packed with laptop-wielding hipsters, leaving little or no room for hotel guests, and there's nowhere else to lounge. The cocktail bar was closed for two of our four days. That left the rooftop bar, which is pleasant, weather permitting, if you can ignore the sour staff.

There's no real restaurant either, just a ground-floor deli and breakfast bar with equally unhappy staff. The continental breakfast included in the rate is meager: drip coffee or tea, orange or grapefruit juice, and one item such as a croissant. Sandwiches are extra. At an average of around $800 a night, you'd think they could throw in a cappuccino, or keep their dignity and not include breakfast at all.

Most of the time there is only one person at the reception desk, which means long queues. This was at its worst when we came back for the luggage we'd left with the hotel after checking out. The unfriendly receptionist told us no one was available to fetch bags from the luggage room and that we'd have to do it ourselves. So six groups of guests trooped up to the second floor to find an office she'd pointed us to, where someone could finally take us to the luggage room.

If you're willing to spend $800 a night, there are far better hotels in New York that offer the same design fix but know a great deal more about amenities and customer service than the Public.

review_text:
My stay at PUBLIC Hotel left a lot to be desired, starting with a frustrating check-in experience. Despite arriving at 3:10 PM (past the 3:00 PM check-in time), I was unable to use the iPad check-in because I hadn't received a room number yet.

When I spoke to the front desk, I was told my room wasn’t ready because the previous guest had a late check-out, and that my personal request for robes and slippers—which I had submitted three weeks in advance—was causing an additional delay.

When I asked for an ETA, I was simply told to come back in 20 minutes. I returned around 3:30pm and spoke with another staff member who gave a vague answer. Given the inconvenient delay that nearly made me late for an uptown reservation at 5pm, I asked if a late check-out could be accommodated for my departure day. I was told they couldn't approve it at the desk and I’d have to call down later. No gesture or accommodation was offered to alleviate the inconvenience, making for a poor first impression.

To top it off, when I finally got to the room, the robes and slippers I requested three weeks prior were missing. When I asked about them later that evening, I was told they were completely out of slippers, though we did eventually receive the robes.

The atmosphere here is immaculate, but unfortunately, the service left a lot to be desired.

My friends and I stopped in on Saturday night, and the place was still lively and packed. After asking our waitress for recommendations, we decided to order a more affordable bottle of pinot. We were surprised when the more expensive gruner was brought to our table instead - and it was served completely warm.

When we tried to clarify the mix-up with our waitress, we felt ignored. The wine was so warm that we repeatedly had to ask for ice just to make it drinkable.

To make matters even stranger, another waiter told us that he wanted to go home and asked if he could give us to-go cups so we could leave, without really offering another option.

I genuinely love the vibe and atmosphere of this place, but if the staff didn’t have the time or capacity to accommodate a full bottle service that night, it would have been better to be upfront about that. Fortunately, they did allow us to finish our remaining food before leaving, but the experience felt rushed and unorganized.

I used to really enjoy dining here. I truly hope management slows down their expansion slightly to refocus on maintaining quality, staffing, and customer service at each individual store.

review_text:
I absolutely love Dudley’s! I come here at least once a month, and it has easily become one of my favorite restaurants over the past 2–3 years. The food, service, and atmosphere are consistently great, and I’ve introduced so many friends to this place.

That being said, I think being such a regular customer allows me to offer some honest feedback.

On one occasion, I found a hair wrapped around my pancake after I had already covered it in syrup and was about to take my first bite. Of course, it was disappointing, but the staff handled it well, replaced my meal, and took it off the bill. Clearly, it didn’t stop me from coming back!

My biggest frustration is the inability to make reservations in the morning. I completely understand how busy brunch can get, especially on weekends and holidays, but I wish there were some flexibility. I tried making a reservation for Mother’s Day because I wanted to bring my mom, but unfortunately, that wasn’t an option.

I also wanted to mention the menu changes following the renovations. The restaurant itself looks beautiful, and I appreciate the updates, but I genuinely miss the original steak frites. It used to be one of my favorite dishes on the menu! While I appreciate the addition of the smothered steak, the changes to the steak frites have been disappointing, and I’ve found myself coming in for dinner much less frequently because of it.

Despite these few critiques, I really do love Dudley’s. It’s a place I consistently return to, recommend to others, and genuinely enjoy supporting. I was just here yesterday and I’m already coming back today!

I hope this feedback is received in the spirit it’s intended. I’m sharing it because I’ve been a loyal customer for years and would love to see a few of the things that originally made this place so special return. Dudley’s is still one of my favorites, and I look forward to many more visits!

review_text:
The Musket Room — An Experience Worth Remembering

For my wife and me, an exceptional dining experience is more than simply a night out. It is something we deliberately save for and look forward to. Our most cherished date nights often combine a Michelin-starred restaurant with a Broadway performance—an opportunity to step away from the demands of everyday life, indulge in something extraordinary, and create lasting memories. We work hard for these moments, and when we choose to spend our hard-earned money on an experience, we hope to leave with something far more meaningful than a wonderful meal.

The Musket Room delivered precisely that.

From the moment we walked through the door, we felt welcomed. Our first interaction was with a gracious, impeccably dressed hostess whose warmth and professionalism immediately set the tone for the evening. The restaurant itself struck a beautiful balance between contemporary sophistication and understated nostalgia. Exposed brick, rich blue leather barstools, thoughtfully spaced tables, and an attentive, polished staff created an atmosphere that felt both intimate and inviting. There was a subtle nod to the Prohibition era, yet the overall aesthetic remained distinctly modern and refined.

The culinary experience was equally impressive. Each course felt intentional, imaginative, and carefully composed. Our introduction to the kitchen's creativity began with sourdough bread accompanied by chicken skin butter—an unexpected and intriguing combination that immediately captured our attention. From that first taste to the final course, the meal remained engaging, with each dish offering something new to appreciate.

The wine pairings further elevated the experience. Our sommelier demonstrated excellent judgment, recommending wines that complemented each course beautifully without overshadowing the cuisine. The thoughtful interplay between food and wine added another dimension to an already memorable evening.

What distinguishes a truly exceptional restaurant, in my opinion, is not merely the quality of its food, the elegance of its surroundings, or the attentiveness of its service. It is the ability to bring all these elements together so seamlessly that guests feel genuinely valued and the evening becomes something worth remembering.

That is exactly what The Musket Room accomplished.

We arrived hoping for a special evening and left with a lasting memory. For two people who treasure these occasional indulgences, there is no greater compliment we can offer.

Thank you to the entire team at The Musket Room for reminding us why experiences like these are worth saving for.

review_text:
This one honestly hurt my heart…

Y’all… this review hurts my heart to write because I am a Sweet Chick fan.

Not a “I tried it once” fan. A real fan.

I’ve been going to Sweet Chick since there was only one location in Brooklyn. I was literally traveling from Jersey to Brooklyn just for the food, the drinks, and the experience, and I never minded doing it because it was always worth it.

So when they opened the Ludlow Street location, I was excited because now I didn’t have to make the trip to Brooklyn every time I wanted my chicken and waffles.

Back then, Sweet Chick was an experience.

They had the big specials board with rotating waffles, desserts, and seasonal items. Their chicken and waffles never missed. I honestly can’t remember ever leaving disappointed.

So this review is really hard for me.

Back on June 26th, after work, my mom and I decided to grab dinner. I work in the LES, and she suggested Sweet Chick. I did tell her my brother Robert had gone recently and said it had changed a lot, but we figured we’d see for ourselves.

We got there around 9-ish.

The first thing we noticed…

It was HOT.

Not warm.

Hot.

Like, “why does it feel like a sauna in here?” hot.

We’ve had enough hot weather this summer, so walking into a restaurant with little to no air conditioning was honestly uncomfortable. We actually debated leaving before we even ordered, but decided to stick it out.

Unfortunately… it never got better.

The service also wasn’t what I remembered.

I’m really big on customer service, and Sweet Chick has always had amazing service whenever I’ve gone. This time it just felt different. The attentiveness wasn’t there, and the overall vibe just felt… off.

Even the menu has changed.

My mom used to love their kale salad, but now it’s made differently with things like dates, and she wasn’t interested in it anymore.

For drinks, my mom ordered an espresso martini, and unfortunately she really didn’t enjoy it. It was pretty bitter, and we couldn’t quite figure out what was off about it. If I’m ordering an espresso martini, I have certain expectations, and this one just didn’t hit for her.

I ordered the Queen of New York, and I actually really enjoyed my drink. No complaints there.

Now… the food.

I ordered the Maple Chipotle Chicken & Sweet Potato Waffle.

And this is where my heart really broke.

Years ago, when they first introduced the sweet potato waffle as a special, I remember it actually tasting like sweet potato.

This one…

Honestly just tasted like a regular waffle.

I kept looking for that sweet potato flavor, and it just wasn’t there.

The chicken itself was crispy and cooked well, but the maple chipotle sauce wasn’t evenly coated. Some bites were really good, while other pieces were dry because they barely had any sauce on them.

Another thing longtime Sweet Chick fans might notice is the butter service.

I remember getting three or four different flavored butters, each in their own little container.

This time we got two flavors together in one cup.

It’s a small thing, but it was one of those details that always made Sweet Chick feel special.

My mom ordered the Carolina BBQ Chicken with the Grilled Corn Waffle.

I’ll be fair—her waffle absolutely tasted like a corn waffle. I tried it, and it was really good.

She enjoyed her meal more than I did, although she also had a few pieces of chicken that weren’t evenly coated with sauce and were a little dry.

Overall, she thought it was okay.

And I think that’s really the word for this visit.

Okay.

Not terrible.

But not the Sweet Chick we remembered.

Maybe that’s why this visit hit me so hard.

When you’ve loved a place for years, you naturally compare it to what you know it can be.

I genuinely hope this was just an off night because I have so many great memories here, and I’d honestly love to come back one day and have the Sweet Chick experience that made me fall in love with it in the first place.

Because this restaurant has meant a lot to me over the years, and I’m rooting for it.

I really am.

I booked Duane Park for my birthday on October 22, but we left before dinner because of how we were treated when we arrived.

Our reservation was at 7:30 p.m. I deliberately arrived about five minutes early because I understood seating was first come, first served, and several tables near the stage were still open. What I didn't know was that arriving early wouldn't count unless my entire party was present. I was told to wait by the entrance, and other parties who arrived after me were seated in the meantime. If seating priority only applies once every guest is present, that should be explained when booking.

My friend was then told by Jonathan, who identified himself as the general manager, to leave his light jacket at the coat check. He took it off but preferred not to check it, and was then told he couldn't enter carrying it: he had to check it or put it back on. My own blazer was also very light, and the whole back-and-forth over coats felt unnecessary and confrontational.

After we sat down, we waited to be acknowledged while nearby tables were attended to. When I asked for a manager and raised these concerns, Jonathan disputed that the jacket instruction had been given.

By then, the hassle at the entrance and the long wait had already spoiled our mood. Instead of a relaxed, welcoming attitude toward guests, we got unnecessary rules and friction. We didn't want to continue the evening in that mood, and we didn't think it would be worth the money, so we left.

The space was also smaller and more cramped than the Instagram photos suggested, with tables very close together and close to the stage.

I can't comment on the food or show since we left before ordering. We found another place that welcomed us warmly, and had a wonderful birthday evening.

review_text:
My husband and I just had lunch on Friday at Edo Ya with Chef Edgar, and wow, what an experience!

First, the ambiance is peaceful and beautiful--great way to have an omakase.

We originally got the 14-course, but ended up changing to the 19-course omakase halfway through because it was amazing!!

As others stated, he sources his fish directly from Japan and all tasted so incredibly fresh.  It started with appetizers including sashimi and lobster.

For the nigiri, the rice is seasoned where it has a little bit of a darker tint (which is usually a good sign that it'll be delicious!), a perfect flavor to accompany the fish.  He took the time to explain each piece of nigiri to us.  It'll always change due to what's available, but our favorites were the Santa Barbara uni, scallop (never had scallop like this before!), seared sole and seared toro collar!

This place ranks in the top omakase experiences we've had in NYC.  Will definitely be back!

I have been coming to this restaurant regularly for lunch, and my previous experiences have always been pleasant. The servers who usually work outside have always been friendly, kind, and welcoming.

Today, however, I had an extremely disappointing experience.

I brought a friend here for the first time and recommended this restaurant, proudly mentioning that it had been around for decades.

At around 2:00 PM, I asked a male server if we could sit outside. He pointed us to an outdoor table. He was a slightly heavyset man with a noticeable belly, wearing a white T-shirt.

From the moment we approached him, his facial expressions and the way he looked us up and down made us feel extremely uncomfortable and unwelcome. After we sat down, we noticed him turning his back toward us and whispering with other staff members. We don’t know what was being said, but the way he looked at and treated us made us feel judged and singled out. We couldn’t help but wonder whether we were being treated differently because we are Asian, or whether my friend was being judged because of their gender identity or appearance.

We felt so uncomfortable that we decided to leave. We politely said, “I’m sorry, we’ll go somewhere else.”

His response was shocking: “That’s okay. My restaurant has money. My restaurant has plenty of money.”

I was honestly speechless. What kind of response is that to customers?

I don’t know whether this employee is a manager or a server, but regardless of his position, such an arrogant and disrespectful attitude is completely unacceptable in the hospitality industry.
